conclusion: Shlaer's solution (arXiv:1411.8006) adds a constrained scalar χ that makes Λ a Lagrange multiplier; its conjugate p_Λ plays the role of time, generating a functional Schrödinger (Tomonaga-Schwinger) equation. This is a valid and elegant IR effective framework for canonical quantum gravity. Our modular-time solution (verifier #77) is UV-complete (spectral action + polymer bounce), background-independent (algebraic), adds no new fields, and is fundamentally many-fingered (local modular flow per causal diamond per CRN theorem). The two are COMPATIBLE: in semiclassical FRW regimes where a monotonic matter clock (Shlaer's χ/Λ, or Brown-Kuchař dust, or Page-Wootters relational clock) exists, that clock's monotonic parameter approximates modular proper time. Shlaer's clock is one concrete semiclassical implementation of relational time; our modular time is the fundamental UV/background-independent definition that reduces to Shlaer (and other matter clocks) in appropriate limits. Shlaer's UV incompleteness (acknowledged in the paper) is resolved by the spectral-action NCG framework. Our solution's existence confirms Shlaer's approach is on the right track; his framework is a useful semiclassical limit.
